nodes.name: Settings
nodes.notes: The only node you edit: your bot token and your Telegram user ID. Never share this workflow while the token is in it.

nodes.name: Ask Telegram for new messages
nodes.notes: Long polling: Telegram holds the request up to 8 s (checks start every 10 s) and answers the moment a message arrives. Nothing on the server is public.

nodes.name: If polling failed: remove old webhook
nodes.notes: Polling fails while a webhook is set on the bot (e.g. from an earlier setup). This removes it, so the next check works.

nodes.name: Keep only my messages
nodes.notes: Ignores everyone except the owner. Returning nothing stops the run quietly when there are no new messages.

nodes.name: Confirm received
nodes.notes: Tells Telegram these messages arrived, BEFORE anything slow happens, so Jarvis can never reply twice.

nodes.name: Listen (speech to text)
nodes.notes: The gateway's 'listen' alias: ElevenLabs Scribe, Groq Whisper as backup. Pick your OpenAI-type credential here.

nodes.name: Prepare each message
nodes.notes: Setup mode, commands (/start, /new) and problems get a direct reply. Text (typed or heard) gets the conversation history and goes to the brain.

nodes.name: Ask Jarvis's brain
nodes.notes: The gateway's 'smart' alias: best free model, automatic fallback. Pick your OpenAI-type credential here: no key is written in the workflow.

nodes.name: Spoken to? Answer by voice too
Speak (text to speech)
nodes.notes: The voice service (Lesson 10): ElevenLabs first, local Piper when free credits run out. Returns a Telegram voice note (OGG).

nodes.name: Send voice note
nodes.notes: If speaking failed there is no audio: this step fails quietly and you still have the text reply.
